agent_answer:

Zoe pushes against the blanket no-work rule by arguing her story is “technically a work story” but “reads as a comedy of errors,” so she thinks the no-work rule has a “humanitarian exception clause.”

The group’s response, via Dan, clarifies the rule’s real purpose: it protects the group from **spreadsheet updates and line-management disputes**. A comedy from A&E is treated as **categorically distinct**.

So the boundary is not “no work talk at all.” It is really about avoiding **boring or draining work admin/conflict**, while entertaining work anecdotes may be allowed.
